focus: Pi OAuth credential store, public API, and auth-file concurrency
instruction: Review the current working tree for the Pi OAuth credential-store fix in mono-agent. Focus on packages/agent-runtime/src/pi-auth.js, packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/providers/pi-native.js, packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/types.js, generated types, and tests. Determine whether the amended fix closes the earlier issues: OAuth credentials preserved instead of coerced to api_key, enhanced readCredential failures are surfaced rather than swallowed, public resolver types support read/modify/delete methods, and concurrent writes across providers cannot lose data within this process. Report only actionable remaining correctness/security/test gaps. If no issue remains for this focus, report none with evidence.
result_json: {"status":"issues","findings":[{"severity":"medium","file":"packages/agent-runtime/src/pi-auth.js","line":104,"title":"Auth-file write queue is keyed by raw path string, so same-file aliases can still lose provider updates","details":"The new in-process serialization works only when every resolver was constructed with the exact same path string. `createPiOAuthApiKeyResolver()` keeps `options.path` unchanged at lines 27-29, and `enqueueAuthFile()` keys `authFileChains` by that raw string at lines 104-110. I verified a same-process race with one resolver using `auth.json` and another using the absolute path to that same file: concurrent `modifyCredential()` calls for providers `a` and `b` left `a.access = \"a-new\"` but reverted `b.access` to the old value. That violates the intended guarantee that concurrent writes across providers cannot lose data within this process whenever the same auth file is reached through common path aliases.","recommended_fix":"Canonicalize the auth file path once when constructing the resolver and use that canonical value for both filesystem operations and the queue key. At minimum use `node:path.resolve()` to freeze relative paths to an absolute path; preferably collapse existing symlinks via `realpath` or a canonicalized parent+basename path. Add a regression test that creates two resolvers for the same auth file via relative and absolute paths, concurrently modifies different providers, and asserts both updates remain."}],"evidence":["`createDynamicCredentialStore()` now preserves OAuth credentials from enhanced `readCredential()` and lets read failures reject instead of warning/swallowing; focused tests cover both paths in `src/__tests__/ai/pi-native.test.js`.","`createPiOAuthApiKeyResolver()` exposes `readCredential`, `modifyCredential`, and `deleteCredential`; generated `types/pi-auth.d.ts` includes those methods on `PiApiKeyResolver`, and `AgentRuntimeHostOptions.resolvePiApiKey` references that type.","Same-string same-file concurrent writes are serialized: `src/__tests__/pi-auth.test.js` covers concurrent refreshes and cross-provider `modifyCredential()` writes for two resolvers using the same `authPath`.","Verification run passed: `pnpm --filter @mono-agent/agent-runtime run test -- src/__tests__/pi-auth.test.js src/__tests__/ai/pi-native.test.js src/__tests__/ai/router.test.js src/__tests__/ai/failure.test.js` completed with 44 test files and 573 tests passing; `pnpm --filter @mono-agent/agent-runtime exec tsc -p tsconfig.types.json --noEmit --pretty false` also passed.","Manual temp-file repro for the remaining race used the same auth file via `auth.json` and its absolute path; after concurrent provider updates, the final JSON retained only one update, confirming the queue-key alias issue."]}

focus: Router failover semantics and failure taxonomy
instruction: Review the current working tree for router/failure-kind behavior. Focus on packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/runtime/router.js, packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/failure.js, packages/agent-runtime/src/ai/providers/pi-native/result-builder.js, packages/observability/src/failure-kinds.ts, summary-schema.ts, types.ts, and related tests. Determine whether provider_auth is consistently preserved for auth-like failures, exhausted availability still reports provider_unavailable_exhausted only after real eligible attempts, and all-skipped/no-execution chains use skipped_capability_mismatch without breaking observability. Report actionable remaining issues only.
